text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's the fishing man. Can you hear me?
B: Hi, yeah. Yeah, I can hear you. I'm Luke.
A: Tracey. I said to myself when I saw your photo, he's got all the gear like my brother. He's got a shed full of rods and boxes, his wife won't go in there.
B: Ha. Yeah, that's the spare room for me. Hannah's given up on it, to be fair.
A: Is that your girlfriend? Hannah?
B: Yeah. Six years. She's a dental nurse.
A: Oh, lovely. So go on, what do you do? Sorry, I've been asking everyone that, I'm like a broken record.
B: No, it's fine. I'm a shift manager at a parcel depot. Early shift, about forty staff.
A: Early as in what?
B: I'm in for half five.
A: Oh, you poor thing. I thought I had it bad. My first aqua's at seven and the pool's always freezing. I'm in there going "keep moving, keep moving", and it's 'cause I'm cold, not them.
B: Ha. You teach in the water?
A: Aqua aerobics, circuits, a seated class for the older ones. Fitness instructor, at a leisure centre in Walsall. I'm sessional, though, so I'm forever chasing a few more hours. I'd love a proper contract, just to know where I am every month, you know?
B: Yeah. I get that. Knowing what's coming in. We're saving for a deposit, and every time we get a bit closer, prices go up again round us. Basingstoke's not even that posh, but it's still mental.
A: It's the same everywhere, bab. Sorry, I call everyone that at work. I rent off the housing association, and I'm just glad it's a fair rent, honestly.
B: No, you're alright.
A: Do you get tired, the early starts? I'd be dead by Thursday.
B: Wednesday, usually. I'm knackered by Wednesday. And it gets worse coming up to Christmas, peak season. That's when I sort of don't sleep. Lot of pressure on numbers, and I don't like pushing the lads harder than is fair. So the fishing's kind of my reset button.
A: That makes sense. I've got my walking group Sunday mornings, up Barr Beacon. Same thing really, you get to the top and you can't worry about nothing, you're too out of breath.
B: Ha, yeah.
A: Did you talk to the Spurs lad? Lewis?
B: Yeah, first round. He seemed alright. Normal bloke.
A: He told me he warms up for five-a-side by kicking a ball about. I told him straight, that's not a warm-up.
B: I used to play. Packed it in after my knee twinged.
A: Did you do any stretching before?
B: Erm. No. Not really.
A: There you go then! You lot. What do you do for your tea of a night, do you cook?
B: When I'm on earlies I do dinner, yeah. Spag bol, chilli, roast chicken. Nothing fancy. And then Friday's a Chinese, same order every time.
A: Same as me! Chippy on a Friday, and if it's a curry I always have the korma. My sister says I'm boring. I say I know what I like.
B: That's what I say. Why change it if it's good.
A: Exactly. My lad Kieran, he's sixteen, he'll eat anything though. I've got to get him to football tonight and he'll want feeding before and after.
B: Does he play for a team?
A: Under-seventeens, local club. He's decent, actually. I'm stood on the side every Saturday in the cold with a flask going—
